dossiers.label: Socrates the midwife
dossiers.about: Socrates, son of the midwife Phaenarete, practises the same art on souls, not bodies: barren of wisdom himself, he delivers young men of their thoughts and tests whether the offspring is a phantom or genuine and true.

passage.end_quote: ψεῦδός τε συγχωρῆσαι καὶ ἀληθὲς ἀφανίσαι οὐδαμῶς θέμις

parts.label: You are in labour, for you are not empty but pregnant
parts.quote: ὠδίνεις γάρ, ὦ φίλε Θεαίτητε, διὰ τὸ μὴ κενὸς ἀλλʼ ἐγκύμων εἶναι

parts.label: Son of a midwife, Phaenarete
parts.quote: ὑὸς μαίας μάλα γενναίας τε καὶ βλοσυρᾶς, Φαιναρέτης

parts.label: Phantom or genuine and true
parts.quote: πότερον εἴδωλον καὶ ψεῦδος ἀποτίκτει τοῦ νέου ἡ διάνοια ἢ γόνιμόν τε καὶ ἀληθές

parts.label: Barren of wisdom; the god compels me to deliver
parts.quote: μαιεύεσθαί με ὁ θεὸς ἀναγκάζει, γεννᾶν δὲ ἀπεκώλυσεν

echoes.quote: ἡ μαιευτικὴ ἡμῖν τέχνη ἀνεμιαῖά φησι γεγενῆσθαι
echoes.why: At the end: our midwife's art declares all these offspring wind-eggs.
Diotima: love is giving birth in beauty, in body and in soul.

related.why: Another image of Socrates' effect: he makes others perplexed.

web.title: Theaetetus (dialogue)
web.quote: Socrates considers his philosophical work as midwifery

dossiers.label: Wonder, the beginning of philosophy
dossiers.about: Theaetetus is dizzy at the puzzles of the dice; Socrates: this feeling, wonder, belongs to the philosopher; philosophy has no other beginning, and whoever made Iris the daughter of Thaumas was no bad genealogist.

passage.start_quote: μάλα γὰρ φιλοσόφου τοῦτο τὸ πάθος, τὸ θαυμάζειν
passage.end_quote: Θαύμαντος ἔκγονον φήσας οὐ κακῶς γενεαλογεῖν

parts.label: Wonder is the philosopher's feeling
parts.quote: μάλα γὰρ φιλοσόφου τοῦτο τὸ πάθος, τὸ θαυμάζειν

parts.label: No other beginning of philosophy
parts.quote: οὐ γὰρ ἄλλη ἀρχὴ φιλοσοφίας ἢ αὕτη

dossiers.label: The digression: the philosopher, Thales, and becoming like god
dossiers.about: The philosopher in court looks ridiculous, like Thales who fell into a well while gazing at the stars and was mocked by a Thracian servant girl. Evils cannot vanish; so we should flee from here to there, and flight is becoming like god so far as possible: to become just and holy with wisdom.

passage.start_quote: οἱ ἐν ταῖς φιλοσοφίαις πολὺν χρόνον διατρίψαντες

parts.label: Philosophers in court look ridiculous
parts.quote: εἰς τὰ δικαστήρια ἰόντες γελοῖοι φαίνονται ῥήτορες

parts.label: Thales in the well and the Thracian girl
parts.quote: Θαλῆν ἀστρονομοῦντα, ὦ Θεόδωρε, καὶ ἄνω βλέποντα, πεσόντα εἰς φρέαρ

parts.label: Evils can never perish
parts.quote: ἀλλʼ οὔτʼ ἀπολέσθαι τὰ κακὰ δυνατόν

parts.label: Flight is becoming like god so far as possible
parts.quote: φυγὴ δὲ ὁμοίωσις θεῷ κατὰ τὸ δυνατόν

parts.label: To become just and holy with wisdom
parts.quote: ὁμοίωσις δὲ δίκαιον καὶ ὅσιον μετὰ φρονήσεως γενέσθαι

echoes.why: The Republic: the gods never neglect one who seeks to become like god by practising virtue.
The cave: the returning philosopher looks ridiculous in the courts below.

related.why: The philosopher who returns to the courts is laughed at.

testimonia.quote: to be assimilated to god, as far as it is possible for a man to be
testimonia.says: Alcinous (ch. 28 in modern numbering) makes likeness to god the end of life, citing the Theaetetus.

web.title: Plato on Knowledge in the Theaetetus

dossiers.label: The wax tablet
dossiers.about: Suppose there is a block of wax in our souls, a gift of Memory, mother of the Muses, larger or smaller, purer or muddier; we stamp on it what we perceive and think, like a signet ring. False belief is fitting a perception to the wrong imprint.

passage.start_quote: θὲς δή μοι λόγου ἕνεκα ἐν ταῖς ψυχαῖς ἡμῶν ἐνὸν κήρινον ἐκμαγεῖον

parts.label: A block of wax in our souls
parts.quote: ἐν ταῖς ψυχαῖς ἡμῶν ἐνὸν κήρινον ἐκμαγεῖον

parts.label: The gift of Memory, mother of the Muses
parts.quote: δῶρον τοίνυν αὐτὸ φῶμεν εἶναι τῆς τῶν Μουσῶν μητρὸς Μνημοσύνης

parts.label: Like the marks of signet rings
Small, muddy or crowded souls judge falsely
parts.quote: πάντες οὖν οὗτοι γίγνονται οἷοι δοξάζειν ψευδῆ

related.why: The next model of false belief, after the wax tablet fails for thought alone.

web.title: Plato on Knowledge in the Theaetetus
web.quote: Fourth Puzzle About False Belief: the Wax Tablet

dossiers.label: The aviary
dossiers.about: Knowledge possessed is not always knowledge held: like a man who keeps wild birds in an aviary, we have caught pieces of knowledge, but must hunt them again to hold them, and may grab a ring-dove for a pigeon, eleven for twelve.

passage.end_quote: ἔγωγε οὐκ ἔχω τί χρὴ λέγειν

parts.label: Wild birds kept in an aviary at home
Possessing is not having in hand
parts.quote: τρόπον μὲν [γὰρ] ἄν πού τινα φαῖμεν αὐτὸν αὐτὰς ἀεὶ ἔχειν

parts.label: A ring-dove for a pigeon: eleven for twelve

related.why: Socrates names both models together when the aviary fails.
